title: DELLA magnitude-aware Mirror delta basis
hypothesis: Magnitude-aware retention followed by shared-basis task codes can preserve task function with fewer complete payload bytes than DELLA-style sparse deltas; gains must exceed random DARE sparsification, TIES and native PCA/shared coding.
physical_object: shared base model and a magnitude-selected sparse task-delta bank
mirror_coordinate: per-task coefficients over a shared PCA basis fitted to magnitude-retained deltas

development.selection_metric: held-out task-output NRMSE, complete serialized bytes, DELLA-relative error and interference

success_gate: At least one PCA rank across all audit seeds: full payload <=75% of magnitude-sparse payload, task-output NRMSE <= magnitude-sparse NRMSE +.02, and active inference arithmetic <=1.25x sparse decode. Mirror-specific value requires strict improvement over canonical native PCA/shared-basis control; exact alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific attribution.
failure_gate: No magnitude-PCA rank meets the frozen bytes/quality/compute gate, or native PCA/shared-basis coding exactly matches the candidate. Report magnitude versus random retention separately.
boundaries: Synthetic low-rank task deltas only; no pretrained fine-tuning or natural benchmark.
Top-magnitude retention is a transparent DELLA-inspired sparsification control, not a reproduction of the full DELLA sampling algorithm.
TIES is reported as a shared merged-model interference point, not as per-task model retention.
No GPU/production runtime claim; compute is an analytic proxy.
